passages.text: On one occasion, while Jesus was standing by the Lake of Gennesaret with the crowd pressing in on Him to hear the word of God, He saw two boats at the edge of the lake. The fishermen had left them and were washing their nets.
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood by the Lake of Gennesaret.
A large crowd pressed in on Jesus.
The people wanted to hear the word of God.
Jesus saw two boats at the edge of the lake.
The fishermen had left the boats.
The fishermen were washing their nets.
passages.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ τὸν ὄχλον ἐπικεῖσθαι αὐτῷ καὶ ἀκούειν τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν ἑστὼς παρὰ τὴν λίμνην Γεννησαρέτ καὶ εἶδεν πλοῖα δύο ἑστῶτα παρὰ τὴν λίμνην οἱ δὲ ἁλιεῖς ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ἀποβάντες ἔπλυνον τὰ δίκτυα

passages.text: Jesus got into the boat belonging to Simon and asked him to put out a little from shore. And sitting down, He taught the people from the boat.
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood by the Lake of Gennesaret.
A large crowd pressed in to hear Him teach the word of God.
Jesus saw two boats at the edge of the lake.
The fishermen had left the boats and were washing their nets.
Jesus got into one of the boats.
This boat belonged to Simon.
Jesus asked Simon to move the boat a little away from the shore.
Jesus sat down in the boat.
Jesus taught the people from the boat.
passages.original: ἐμβὰς δὲ εἰς ἓν τῶν πλοίων ὃ ἦν Σίμωνος ἠρώτησεν αὐτὸν ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ἐπαναγαγεῖν ὀλίγον καθίσας δὲ ἐκ τοῦ πλοίου ἐδίδασκεν τοὺς ὄχλους

passages.text: When Jesus had finished speaking, He said to Simon, “Put out into deep water and let down your nets for a catch.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus finished speaking to the people.
He spoke to Simon.
Jesus said, “Go out into deep water.
Let down your nets.
You will catch fish.”
passages.original: Ὡς δὲ ἐπαύσατο λαλῶν εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν Σίμωνα Ἐπανάγαγε εἰς τὸ βάθος καὶ χαλάσατε τὰ δίκτυα ὑμῶν εἰς ἄγραν

passages.text: “Master,” Simon replied, “we have worked hard all night without catching anything. But because You say so, I will let down the nets.”
passages.sermon:
Simon was a fisherman.
Jesus spoke to Simon.
Simon answered Jesus.
Simon called Jesus “Master.”
Simon said, “We worked hard all night.”
Simon said, “We did not catch anything.”
Simon said, “But you told me to let down the nets.”
Simon said, “I will let down the nets because you say so.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς Σίμων εἶπεν Ἐπιστάτα δι’ ὅλης νυκτὸς κοπιάσαντες οὐδὲν ἐλάβομεν ἐπὶ δὲ τῷ ῥήματί σου χαλάσω τὰ δίκτυα

passages.text: When they had done so, they caught such a large number of fish that their nets began to tear.
passages.sermon:
Simon and his companions obeyed Jesus.
They let down their nets into the deep water.
They caught a very large number of fish.
Their nets began to tear.
passages.original: καὶ τοῦτο ποιήσαντες συνέκλεισαν πλῆθος ἰχθύων πολύ διερρήσσετο δὲ τὰ δίκτυα αὐτῶν

passages.text: So they signaled to their partners in the other boat to come and help them, and they came and filled both boats so full that they began to sink.
passages.sermon:
Simon and his companions were fishermen.
They caught a huge number of fish.
Their nets began to break.
They signaled to their partners in the other boat.
They asked them to come and help.
The partners came.
They filled both boats with fish.
Both boats became so full that they began to sink.
passages.original: καὶ κατένευσαν τοῖς μετόχοις ἐν τῷ ἑτέρῳ πλοίῳ τοῦ ἐλθόντας συλλαβέσθαι αὐτοῖς καὶ ἦλθον καὶ ἔπλησαν ἀμφότερα τὰ πλοῖα ὥστε βυθίζεσθαι αὐτά

passages.text: When Simon Peter saw this, he fell at Jesus’ knees. “Go away from me, Lord,” he said, “for I am a sinful man.”
passages.sermon:
Simon Peter was a fisherman.
Simon Peter saw the great catch of fish.
Simon Peter fell at Jesus’ knees.
Simon Peter said, “Go away from me, Lord.”
Simon Peter said, “I am a sinful man.”
passages.original: Ἰδὼν δὲ Σίμων Πέτρος προσέπεσεν τοῖς γόνασιν Ἰησοῦ λέγων Ἔξελθε ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ ὅτι ἀνὴρ ἁμαρτωλός εἰμι Κύριε

passages.text: For he and his companions were astonished at the catch of fish they had taken, and so were his partners James and John, the sons of Zebedee. “Do not be afraid,” Jesus said to Simon. “From now on you will catch men.”
passages.sermon:
Simon Peter was a fisherman.
He had companions with him.
They caught a large number of fish.
Simon and his companions were amazed at this catch.
James and John were also there.
James and John were sons of Zebedee.
James and John were partners with Simon.
They were also amazed.
Jesus spoke to Simon.
Jesus said, “Do not be afraid.”
Jesus said, “From now on you will catch people.”
passages.original: θάμβος γὰρ περιέσχεν αὐτὸν καὶ πάντας τοὺς σὺν αὐτῷ ἐπὶ τῇ ἄγρᾳ τῶν ἰχθύων ὧν συνέλαβον ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάννην υἱοὺς Ζεβεδαίου οἳ ἦσαν κοινωνοὶ τῷ Σίμωνι Καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν Σίμωνα ὁ Ἰησοῦς Μὴ φοβοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν ἀνθρώπους ἔσῃ ζωγρῶν

passages.text: And when they had brought their boats ashore, they left everything and followed Him.
passages.sermon:
Simon Peter and his companions were fishermen.
They brought their boats to the shore.
They left everything behind.
They followed Jesus.
passages.original: καὶ καταγαγόντες τὰ πλοῖα ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἀφέντες πάντα ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ

passages.text: While Jesus was in one of the towns, a man came along who was covered with leprosy. When he saw Jesus, he fell facedown and begged Him, “Lord, if You are willing, You can make me clean.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was in a town.
A man came to Jesus.
This man had leprosy all over his body.
The man saw Jesus.
He fell down with his face to the ground.
He begged Jesus.
He said, “Lord, if you are willing, you can make me clean.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ εἶναι αὐτὸν ἐν μιᾷ τῶν πόλεων καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ πλήρης λέπρας ἰδὼν δὲ τὸν Ἰησοῦν πεσὼν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον ἐδεήθη αὐτοῦ λέγων Κύριε ἐὰν θέλῃς δύνασαί με καθαρίσαι

passages.text: Jesus reached out His hand and touched the man. “I am willing,” He said. “Be clean!” And immediately the leprosy left him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw a man with leprosy.
Jesus reached out His hand.
Jesus touched the man.
Jesus said, “I am willing.”
Jesus said, “Be clean!”
Immediately, the leprosy left the man.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα ἥψατο αὐτοῦ λέγων Θέλω καθαρίσθητι καὶ εὐθέως ἡ λέπρα ἀπῆλθεν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: “Do not tell anyone,” Jesus instructed him. “But go, show yourself to the priest and present the offering Moses prescribed for your cleansing, as a testimony to them.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the man who had been healed of leprosy.
Jesus gave him instructions.
Jesus said, “Do not tell anyone.”
Jesus said, “Go to the priest.”
Jesus said, “Show yourself to the priest.”
Jesus said, “Give the offering Moses commanded for your cleansing.”
Jesus said, “This will be a testimony to them.”
passages.original: Καὶ αὐτὸς παρήγγειλεν αὐτῷ μηδενὶ εἰπεῖν Ἀλλὰ ἀπελθὼν δεῖξον σεαυτὸν τῷ ἱερεῖ καὶ προσένεγκε περὶ τοῦ καθαρισμοῦ σου καθὼς προσέταξεν Μωϋσῆς εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς

passages.text: But the news about Jesus spread all the more, and great crowds came to hear Him and to be healed of their sicknesses.
passages.sermon:
Jesus healed a man with leprosy.
People heard about Jesus healing the man.
News about Jesus spread quickly.
Many people learned what Jesus had done.
Large crowds gathered to see Jesus.
The crowds wanted to hear Jesus teach.
The crowds wanted Jesus to heal their sicknesses.
passages.original: Διήρχετο δὲ μᾶλλον ὁ λόγος περὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ συνήρχοντο ὄχλοι πολλοὶ ἀκούειν καὶ θεραπεύεσθαι ἀπὸ τῶν ἀσθενειῶν αὐτῶν

passages.text: Yet He frequently withdrew to the wilderness to pray.
passages.sermon: Jesus often went away from the crowds.\r\nHe went into the wilderness.\r\nHe prayed there.
passages.original: αὐτὸς δὲ ἦν ὑποχωρῶν ἐν ταῖς ἐρήμοις καὶ προσευχόμενος

passages.text: One day Jesus was teaching, and the Pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting there. People had come from Jerusalem and from every village of Galilee and Judea, and the power of the Lord was present for Him to heal the sick.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was teaching one day.
The Pharisees were there.
The teachers of the law were also there.
They had come from every village of Galilee.
They had come from Judea.
They had come from Jerusalem.
The power of the Lord was with Jesus.
He had power to heal the sick.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν μιᾷ τῶν ἡμερῶν καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν διδάσκων καὶ ἦσαν καθήμενοι Φαρισαῖοι καὶ νομοδιδάσκαλοι οἳ ἦσαν ἐληλυθότες ἐκ πάσης κώμης τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ Ἰουδαίας καὶ Ἰερουσαλήμ καὶ δύναμις Κυρίου ἦν εἰς τὸ ἰᾶσθαι αὐτόν

passages.text: Just then some men came carrying a paralyzed man on a mat. They tried to bring him inside to set him before Jesus, but they could not find a way through the crowd. So they went up on the roof and lowered him on his mat through the tiles into the middle of the crowd, right in front of Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Some men came.
They carried a man who could not walk.
He lay on a mat.
They wanted to bring him inside.
They wanted to place him in front of Jesus.
They could not find a way through the crowd.
So they went up on the roof.
They made an opening through the tiles.
They lowered the man on his mat.
They placed him in the middle of the crowd.
They set him right in front of Jesus.
passages.original: Καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνδρες φέροντες ἐπὶ κλίνης ἄνθρωπον ὃς ἦν παραλελυμένος καὶ ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν εἰσενεγκεῖν καὶ θεῖναι αὐτὸν ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ καὶ μὴ εὑρόντες ποίας εἰσενέγκωσιν αὐτὸν διὰ τὸν ὄχλον ἀναβάντες ἐπὶ τὸ δῶμα διὰ τῶν κεράμων καθῆκαν αὐτὸν σὺν τῷ κλινιδίῳ εἰς τὸ μέσον ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: When Jesus saw their faith, He said, “Friend, your sins are forgiven.”
passages.sermon: Jesus saw their faith.\r\nHe spoke to the paralyzed man.\r\nHe said, “Friend, your sins are forgiven.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἰδὼν τὴν πίστιν αὐτῶν εἶπεν Ἄνθρωπε ἀφέωνταί σοι αἱ ἁμαρτίαι σου

passages.text: But the scribes and Pharisees began thinking to themselves, “Who is this man who speaks blasphemy? Who can forgive sins but God alone?”
passages.sermon:
The scribes and the Pharisees were religious leaders.
They began to think to themselves.
They said, “Who is this man?”
They said, “He speaks blasphemy.”
They said, “Only God can forgive sins.”
They asked, “Who can forgive sins except God alone?”
passages.original: Καὶ ἤρξαντο διαλογίζεσθαι οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι λέγοντες Τίς ἐστιν οὗτος ὃς λαλεῖ βλασφημίας τίς δύναται ἁμαρτίας ἀφεῖναι εἰ μὴ μόνος ὁ Θεός

passages.text: Knowing what they were thinking, Jesus replied, “Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?
passages.sermon: Jesus knew what the scribes and Pharisees were thinking.\r\nHe answered them directly.\r\nHe said, “Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?”
passages.original: Ἐπιγνοὺς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοὺς διαλογισμοὺς αὐτῶν ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Τί διαλογίζεσθε ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν

passages.text: Which is easier: to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up and walk?’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the scribes and Pharisees.
Jesus asked them a question.
He said, “Which is easier to say?”
He gave two options.
The first option is, ‘Your sins are forgiven.’
The second option is, ‘Get up and walk?’”
passages.original: τί ἐστιν εὐκοπώτερον εἰπεῖν Ἀφέωνταί σοι αἱ ἁμαρτίαι σου ἢ εἰπεῖν Ἔγειρε καὶ περιπάτει

passages.text: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on the earth to forgive sins...” He said to the paralytic, “I tell you, get up, pick up your mat, and go home.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of Man.
Jesus has authority on earth to forgive sins.
Jesus wanted people to know this.
Jesus spoke to the paralyzed man.
Jesus said, “I tell you, get up.”
Jesus said, “Pick up your mat.”
Jesus said, “Go home.”
passages.original: ἵνα δὲ εἰδῆτε ὅτι ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐξουσίαν ἔχει ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἀφιέναι ἁμαρτίας εἶπεν τῷ παραλελυμένῳ Σοὶ λέγω ἔγειρε καὶ ἄρας τὸ κλινίδιόν σου πορεύου εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου

passages.text: And immediately the man stood up before them, took what he had been lying on, and went home glorifying God.
passages.sermon:
Jesus healed a paralyzed man.
The man had been unable to walk.
Immediately, the man stood up in front of everyone.
He picked up the mat he had been lying on.
He went to his home.
He glorified God as he went.
passages.original: Καὶ παραχρῆμα ἀναστὰς ἐνώπιον αὐτῶν ἄρας ἐφ’ ὃ κατέκειτο ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ δοξάζων τὸν Θεόν

passages.text: Everyone was taken with amazement and glorified God. They were filled with awe and said, “We have seen remarkable things today.”
passages.sermon:
Everyone saw what happened.
Everyone felt great amazement.
Everyone praised God.
Everyone was filled with awe.
Everyone said, “We have seen remarkable things today.”
passages.original: καὶ ἔκστασις ἔλαβεν ἅπαντας καὶ ἐδόξαζον τὸν Θεόν καὶ ἐπλήσθησαν φόβου λέγοντες ὅτι Εἴδομεν παράδοξα σήμερον

passages.text: After this, Jesus went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax booth. “Follow Me,” He told him, and Levi got up, left everything, and followed Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus went out after these things.
He saw a tax collector.
The tax collector’s name was Levi.
Levi was sitting at the tax booth.
Jesus spoke to Levi.
Jesus said, “Follow Me.”
Levi got up.
Levi left everything.
Levi followed Jesus.
passages.original: Καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ἐξῆλθεν καὶ ἐθεάσατο τελώνην ὀνόματι Λευὶν καθήμενον ἐπὶ τὸ τελώνιον καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ἀκολούθει μοι καὶ καταλιπὼν πάντα ἀναστὰς ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ

passages.text: Then Levi hosted a great banquet for Jesus at his house. A large crowd of tax collectors was there, along with others who were eating with them.
passages.sermon:
Levi was a tax collector.
Levi invited Jesus to his house.
Levi prepared a great banquet for Jesus.
Many tax collectors came to the banquet.
Many other people also came.
These people ate together with Jesus and Levi.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐποίησεν δοχὴν μεγάλην Λευὶς αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἦν ὄχλος πολὺς τελωνῶν καὶ ἄλλων οἳ ἦσαν μετ’ αὐτῶν κατακείμενοι

passages.text: But the Pharisees and their scribes complained to Jesus’ disciples, “Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?”
passages.sermon:
The Pharisees were religious leaders.
The scribes were experts in the law.
The Pharisees and their scribes spoke to Jesus’ disciples.
They complained to the disciples.
They said, “Why do you eat with tax collectors?”
They also said, “Why do you drink with sinners?”
passages.original: καὶ ἐγόγγυζον οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς αὐτῶν πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ λέγοντες Διὰ τί μετὰ τῶν τελωνῶν καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν ἐσθίετε καὶ πίνετε

passages.text: Jesus answered, “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Pharisees and their scribes.
He answered their question.
He said, “Healthy people do not need a doctor.
Sick people need a doctor.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν οἱ ὑγιαίνοντες ἰατροῦ ἀλλὰ οἱ κακῶς ἔχοντες

passages.text: I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners, to repentance.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Pharisees and their scribes.
Jesus said, “I have not come to call righteous people.
I have come to call sinners.
I call sinners to repentance.”
passages.original: οὐκ ἐλήλυθα καλέσαι δικαίους ἀλλὰ ἁμαρτωλοὺς εἰς μετάνοιαν

passages.text: Then they said to Him, “John’s disciples and those of the Pharisees frequently fast and pray, but Yours keep on eating and drinking.”
passages.sermon:
Some people spoke to Jesus.
They said, “John’s disciples fast often.
They pray often.
The disciples of the Pharisees do the same.
But your disciples eat and drink.”
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν πρὸς αὐτόν Οἱ μαθηταὶ Ἰωάννου νηστεύουσιν πυκνὰ καὶ δεήσεις ποιοῦνται ὁμοίως καὶ οἱ τῶν Φαρισαίων οἱ δὲ σοὶ ἐσθίουσιν καὶ πίνουσιν

passages.text: Jesus replied, “Can you make the guests of the bridegroom fast while He is with them?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to them.
Jesus is the Son of God.
He answered their question.
He said, “You cannot make the guests of the bridegroom fast while the bridegroom is with them.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Μὴ δύνασθε τοὺς υἱοὺς τοῦ νυμφῶνος ἐν ᾧ ὁ νυμφίος μετ’ αὐτῶν ἐστιν ποιῆσαι νηστεῦσαι

passages.text: But the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them; then they will fast.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He called Himself the bridegroom.
He said the bridegroom is now with His friends.
He said a time will come.
He said the bridegroom will be taken away from His friends.
He said then His friends will fast in those days.
passages.original: ἐλεύσονται δὲ ἡμέραι καὶ ὅταν ἀπαρθῇ ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ὁ νυμφίος τότε νηστεύσουσιν ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις

passages.text: He also told them a parable: “No one tears a piece of cloth from a new garment and sews it on an old one. If he does, he will tear the new garment as well, and the patch from the new will not match the old.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to them.
He told them a parable.
No one takes a piece of cloth from a new garment.
No one sews that piece on an old garment.
If someone does this, he will tear the new garment.
The patch from the new garment will not match the old garment.
passages.original: Ἔλεγεν δὲ καὶ παραβολὴν πρὸς αὐτοὺς ὅτι Οὐδεὶς ἐπίβλημα ἀπὸ ἱματίου καινοῦ σχίσας ἐπιβάλλει ἐπὶ ἱμάτιον παλαιόν εἰ δὲ μή¦γε καὶ τὸ καινὸν σχίσει καὶ τῷ παλαιῷ οὐ συμφωνήσει τὸ ἐπίβλημα τὸ ἀπὸ τοῦ καινοῦ

passages.text: And no one pours new wine into old wineskins. If he does, the new wine will burst the skins, the wine will spill, and the wineskins will be ruined.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He used a parable to teach them.
No one pours new wine into old wineskins.
If someone pours new wine into old wineskins, the new wine will burst the skins.
The wine will spill.
The wineskins will be ruined.
passages.original: Καὶ οὐδεὶς βάλλει οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς παλαιούς εἰ δὲ μή¦γε ῥήξει ὁ οἶνος ὁ νέος τοὺς ἀσκούς καὶ αὐτὸς ἐκχυθήσεται καὶ οἱ ἀσκοὶ ἀπολοῦνται

passages.text: Instead, new wine is poured into new wineskins.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke a parable to the people.
He said, "People must put new wine into new wineskins."
New wine does not go into old wineskins.
New wineskins are needed for new wine.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς καινοὺς βλητέον

passages.text: And no one after drinking old wine wants new, for he says, ‘The old is better.’ ”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke about people’s choices.\r\nHe said, “No one who has drunk old wine wants new wine.\r\nHe says, ‘The old wine is good.’”
passages.original: καὶ οὐδεὶς πιὼν παλαιὸν θέλει νέον λέγει γάρ Ὁ παλαιὸς χρηστός ἐστιν
